notable_absence.finding: No role or privilege is stated anywhere on this page for creating a child mapping - only the Search Service being enabled, an existing index, an existing type mapping, and being logged in are listed as prerequisites. Same open gap as create-type-mapping.md and create-child-field.md in this batch.

cross_component_finding: This page states directly, in its own words, the hierarchy the round briefing asked about: 'Both child mappings and type mappings use child fields to add and remove fields from a Search index.' This confirms create-child-mapping.md and create-child-field.md are two distinct levels of ONE mapping hierarchy rather than two competing mechanisms - a type mapping (create-type-mapping.md) or a child mapping (this page) is a CONTAINER that is populated by child fields (create-child-field.md), and a child mapping is itself created ON a document field that holds a nested JSON object (making it structurally a specialization of a type mapping's own field-mapping mechanism, one level deeper). No relation predicate in the current registry cleanly expresses 'X is populated by child instances of Y' at the sub-page granularity without also implying full component/sub-component architecture (hasInternalComponent is scoped to services/components, not mapping structure), so I have deliberately NOT minted a new predicate for this and instead record the fact here in plain language plus the verbatim quote above, for reconciliation to decide whether a new predicate (e.g. containsChildElement) is warranted across the whole mapping-hierarchy concept family (search:type-mapping, search:object-mapping, search:xattrs-mapping, search:field-mapping) rather than one-off per this page.
